text:
Cam Talbot's record is 5-3-0 and his save rate is .906, numbers that look ordinary until you see what he has been facing. He has saved 5.3 goals above expected, which means he has kept out 5.3 more goals than the shots against him would usually allow, 85th percentile among goalies. That is a long way from last season, when he finished 13.7 goals below expected in 34 games, and a reminder of how much a goalie's results swing from year to year.

The work has come on the hard shots: .765 on high-danger chances against a league .685. The one thing to watch is rebounds. 12.8% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.8%, and that's the kind of habit that can catch up with a goalie. His start was rough (pulled after six goals against Florida on Oct. 13), and since then he has been above expected in most of his games. He has made nine appearances for Columbus, and CBS Sports summed up his last one, a loss to Florida on Nov. 10, as getting "little help."
